name: Earn veterancy
summary: A unit grows stronger during one life by fighting. Kills, and in some games damage dealt or taken or simply time near the enemy, fill an experience count, and each threshold promotes it a rank. Ranks add health, damage, fire rate, accuracy, speed or self-healing, and some units get a better weapon or a new ability at the top rank. The rank shows on the unit, so enemies know who is dangerous, and it is lost when the unit dies, which makes veterans precious and killing them worth more. Twists include picking a bonus at each promotion, officers whose rank strengthens the troops around them, a rank that a surviving pilot carries into a new vehicle, and killers who take their victim's ranks.
counterplay: Focus the veteran: its rank is on show, and one kill erases everything it built up.
Don't feed it: pull back the cheap, fragile units it would farm for quick promotions (Supreme Commander players even scrap their own to deny it).
Trade early, before it ranks up, while it is still a stock unit.
Use its hard counter: ranks raise its numbers but rarely change what it can hit or resist.
Where progress changes hands on death, take it: kill a sword collector with the same kind of sword to take its heads, or grab the power cubes or evolved armour the veteran leaves behind.

other_examples.note: Destroying enemies worth more than three times its own price makes a unit Veteran, then Elite. Veteran gives one fixed boost to firepower, toughness, speed and how fast the unit shoots; Elite adds self-healing and, on many units, an improved weapon (elite GIs shoot further than a Sentry Gun reaches, and elite Tesla Troopers' bolts chain on to further targets). Crates hand out ranks too, while infantry riding an IFV never rank up, because the vehicle does the shooting.

Three ranks that each add something different: more damage, then more health, then more range, sight and speed, immunity to some effects and self-healing at the top. A ranked victim gives whoever kills it more experience than a fresh one.

Three ranks from the value of what a unit destroys, with health regeneration at the top two. A destroyed US vehicle's pilot climbs out carrying its rank and adds it to the next vehicle he enters; some units rank up by stealing money or capturing buildings, and GLA salvage crates can promote.

Experience is counted from how much damage a unit does, not from who lands the killing shot, and top-rank units heal themselves and fire with a coloured glow, so their rank is easy to spot in a fight.

US units rank up through kills; Panzer Elite units share experience with friends nearby and choose an offensive or a defensive bonus at each level; and the British rank up only their officers and a command tank, which take in the experience of the troops around them and strengthen those troops in return. The fourth army, the Wehrmacht, earns no experience at all and buys its ranks instead, which is not this pattern.

Every army now earns ranks in combat, and experience also comes from damage measured against the target's price, so infantry who wound a tank gain a lot at once. Ranks bring unit-specific bonuses and abilities, they are lost with the unit, and one army has five ranks instead of three.

Five levels earned by kills alone. Each one adds a slice of maximum health and faster regeneration, with a one-off heal on promotion, so a huge unit can feed on cheap ones to stay alive, and players destroy their own cheap units to keep it from doing so.

Experience comes from taking or dealing damage, from kills (more for pricier victims) and even from being close to the enemy. It improves the crew, not the armour: faster aiming and reloading, better accuracy and spotting, and steadier nerves under fire. In skirmish it does not outlast the battle.

shooter_analogues.note: Each kill with the sword adds a head that gives a little more health and speed, up to a cap. Every head goes when its owner dies, a sword user who kills another takes the victim's whole collection, and the sword starts its owner with less health than usual.
In a top-down shooter mode, cubes taken from defeated players or broken boxes each raise health and damage until the match ends, and a player who falls drops part of their stack for others to take.

Body armour that levels up as its wearer deals damage (damage to computer-run enemies counts only in part), and an evolved shield can be looted from a fallen player, so the progress changes hands. The page says it has since left the battle royale mode.

sources.title: Gear (Evo Shield section), Apex Legends Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: For contrast: a run of kills without a death usually unlocks call-ins, which sit closer to the kill-charge resource and the ultimate kind, but in the Sharpshooter party mode a streak hands out stacking perks instead, which is this pattern.

player_translation.summary: Per-life ranks earned in combat that make the player visibly stronger until they die. Assists and damage count, so teamwork pays, while visible chevrons and a bounty on veterans give the enemy a clear target and a way back into the match.
as_user: Kills, assists and damage on enemies fill a rank bar; at each threshold you are promoted, two or three times at most in one life.
Each rank is a small, steady lift (a little more health, faster fire or reload, better aim), and on some units the top rank brings a new weapon or ability. It all lasts until you die.
Staying alive starts to matter: a veteran backs off to heal instead of trading blows, because death resets the bar.
With the elite-weapon variant the top rank changes how you fight, as when the Slave Miner's machine gun becomes a cannon.
as_target: Chevrons over an enemy show its rank; a ranked enemy is worth more to kill, and in some variants it drops a prize.
Focus the veteran with your team, and stop feeding it easy kills.
A rank doesn't change a unit's counters: your anti-armour still beats a ranked tank.
teammates: Assists and damage count, so teammates who soften a target rank up too, and healers and repairers keep the team's veteran alive.
In the shared-experience form nearby allies rank up together, which keeps groups together.
The other team gains from working together as well: marking and focusing the veteran pays all of them through the bounty.
controls: No key: ranks are passive and the rank bar fills by itself.
Elite-weapon variant: at the top rank the main weapon changes in place, on the same button.
Pick-a-bonus variant: at a promotion, a two-choice prompt waits until you are out of combat, and you pick with left or right mouse.
No variant adds a counted key.
feedback: Rank chevrons on the unit and on its nameplate, readable from above, and a promotion flash and sound for everyone nearby, like Red Alert 2's promotion call.
A rank bar in the HUD; the kill feed shows promotions and the bounty paid when a veteran falls.
Top-rank weapons get a distinct colour or glow so enemies notice the change, as heroic units' shots do in Tiberium Wars.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS every unit ranks up and the player tends a whole army; here each player is one unit, so ranks must be few, reachable within a single life, and modest.
RTS ranks mostly come from the value of what a unit kills; in a team shooter, assists and damage should count too (as in Tiberium Wars and Company of Heroes 2), so supporting players aren't left out.
Add a bounty or a dropped prize so that killing a veteran pays back (Eyelander heads, Showdown cubes): a built-in comeback against snowballing.
Keep the stat lifts small and the same for every unit; Red Alert 2's elite self-healing and new weapons become variants for particular units, not a rule for all.
Damp feeding: scale experience by the victim's tier or price, so big units can't farm cheap ones.

team_play.notes: Ranks are personal, but counted assists and shared experience pull teammates in, healers guard the veteran, and the enemy team has to coordinate focus fire and stop feeding it.

notes: A counter per player, thresholds and stat multipliers are simple.
Counting assists and damage needs a record of who damaged whom.
UI: chevrons, a rank bar and promotion effects; elite weapons add content for each unit that has one.
Snowballing: whoever wins the early fights keeps winning; keep the lifts small and pay bounties.
Feeding on cheap units; scale experience by the victim's price or tier.
Veterans may hide to protect their rank instead of playing the objective; give experience for objective play too.
Chevrons read well from above, but the strength behind a rank is invisible, so the lifts should be uniform.
A sudden top-rank weapon change can surprise enemies unless its look changes too.

variants.name: Stat ladder
variants.summary: Two or three ranks from kills and assists, each a small fixed lift to health, damage or fire rate, all lost on death.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 and 3, Supreme Commander, Company of Heroes (US army)

variants.name: Veteran self-repair
variants.summary: The top rank adds slow self-healing out of combat, so a veteran that pulls back returns whole.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Elite, Generals Elite and Heroic, Red Alert 3 Heroic, Supreme Commander levels

variants.name: Experience from damage
variants.summary: Experience comes from damage dealt, and sometimes taken or from time spent near the enemy, rather than from kills, so focus fire and support pay and stealing the last hit doesn't.
variants.seen_in: Tiberium Wars, Company of Heroes 2, Wargame, Apex Legends Evo Shield

variants.name: Elite weapon
variants.summary: At the top rank the main weapon is replaced by a stronger or different one, such as a cannon in place of a machine gun or a bolt that jumps between targets.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 elite weapons (Slave Miner, War Miner, Tesla Trooper, GI)

variants.name: Pick a bonus
variants.summary: At each promotion the player picks an offensive or a defensive bonus, shaping the unit for the fight at hand.

variants.name: Take their trophies
variants.summary: Ranks are trophies: when a ranked unit dies its killer takes some or all of them, or they drop as a pickup, so hunting veterans is the comeback.
variants.seen_in: Team Fortress 2 Eyelander heads, Brawl Stars Showdown power cubes, Apex Legends Evo Shield

adds_strengths.why: Killing a ranked enemy hands it the victim's trophies, so one good kill can rank it up at once.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its own trophies go to whoever kills it, which makes it the bounty everyone hunts.

variants.name: Officer rank
variants.summary: The unit ranks up from the experience of the troops near it and turns its rank into an aura that makes them stronger.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes British Lieutenant and Captain

adds_strengths.why: Its rank also strengthens the teammates around it, and their fighting ranks it up.

adds_weaknesses.why: It must stay near the fight to rank up and boost others, and losing it drops the whole group's bonus.

variants.name: Rank survives the vehicle
variants.summary: When the vehicle is destroyed, its surviving pilot keeps the rank and brings it to the next vehicle they take.

adds_strengths.why: Grows tougher and deadlier with every rank it earns in a life, so a survivor becomes a real threat.

adds_weaknesses.why: Starts each life as a stock unit and loses every rank on death, and its rank marks it as the target to focus.

countered_by.why: Long-range picks can remove a ranked unit before it trades, wiping out everything it built up.
Marking the veteran lets the whole team focus it before it can pull back.

open_questions: Does every Shamble Frontlines unit rank up, as in Red Alert 2 and 3, or only units whose card carries this pattern? If ranks are game-wide, the pattern should only carry special rank rewards such as the elite weapon, and its generic flag should be looked at again.
What earns experience: kills only, or assists, damage and objective play too?
Should a veteran's death pay a bounty to the killer's team, or drop the progress as a pickup?
How many ranks, and how big a lift for each?

Ranks that are bought or come ready-made are left out of this pattern, because no unit earns them during its life: the Company of Heroes Wehrmacht earns no experience and instead buys upgrades at one building, each promoting every existing and future unit in one group (such as all infantry or all tanks); Red Alert 3's captured Veteran Academies and Red Alert 2's Spy inside an enemy factory make later-built units start ranked; and some Generals general's powers let units be built ranked. Should the Wehrmacht kind, a mid-life purchase that reaches units already in the field, go to upgrade-in-field, and the start-ranked kind become a buy-screen option?

shooter_fit.reason: Cheap and readable, and per-life power from kills already exists in shooters (Eyelander heads, Showdown power cubes, Evo shields), but it snowballs in team fights unless the lifts stay small and veterans pay a bounty.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. Nothing was found wrong.
